monet-arrival-of-the-normandy-train-gare.fact: The word “Impressionism” comes from the title of Monet’s painting Impression, Sunrise, shown in 1874.

renoir-lunch-at-the-restaurant-fournaise.fact: Three friends lunch at the Maison Fournaise, on the Île des Impressionnistes in the Seine at Chatou, west of Paris.

cassatt-on-a-balcony.fact: Born in Pennsylvania, Cassatt lived most of her life in France, befriended Degas and exhibited with the Impressionists.

seurat-a-sunday-on-la-grande-jatte-1884.fact: Painted from 1884 to 1886, it is a founding work of neo-impressionism and a leading example of pointillism.

caillebotte-paris-street-rainy-day.fact: The crossing is today’s Place de Dublin, part of the Paris rebuilt under Napoleon III and Haussmann.

degas-the-millinery-shop.fact: At 100 × 110.7 cm, it is the largest work Degas made on the subject of milliners.

hokusai-the-great-wave-off-kanagawa.fact: Look for the three boats beneath the wave, and Mount Fuji, small in the background.

monet-stacks-of-wheat.fact: One of 25 canvases Monet began at the end of summer 1890 and kept painting through the following spring.

renoir-two-sisters.fact: Renoir called it Two Sisters; its first owner, the dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, named it On the Terrace.

homer-the-herring-net.fact: Winslow Homer is best known for his marine subjects.

van-gogh-the-poet-s-garden.fact: Van Gogh made about 2,100 artworks in just over a decade, most of them in the last two years of his life.

gauguin-te-burao.fact: Only moderately successful in his lifetime, Gauguin is now celebrated for his experimental use of color.

gauguin-mahana-no-atua.fact: Gauguin was also a sculptor, printmaker, ceramist and writer, and an influential maker of woodcuts.

gauguin-arlesiennes.fact: Gauguin’s work belongs to the Post-Impressionist and Symbolist movements.

monet-cliff-walk-at-pourville.fact: Two girls in summer sun, fishing boats on the horizon: leisure set against labor.

monet-the-beach-at-sainte-adresse.fact: Painted in 1867, it was first exhibited in 1876, to favorable reactions.

monet-branch-of-the-seine-near-giverny.fact: Monet was Impressionism’s most consistent practitioner of painting landscapes outdoors, en plein air.

monet-on-the-bank-of-the-seine-bennecour.fact: Also called River Scene at Bennecourt; painted in 1868 and given to the Art Institute by the Palmer family in 1922.

monet-bordighera.fact: Monet is seen as a key precursor to modernism, for trying to paint nature as he perceived it.

monet-water-lily-pond.fact: Monet painted about 250 Water Lilies over his last 31 years, many while suffering from cataracts.

pissarro-haymaking-at-eragny.fact: Pissarro was born on the island of Saint Thomas.

pissarro-rabbit-warren-at-pontoise-snow.fact: Pissarro took up the Neo-Impressionist style at 54, working alongside Seurat and Signac.

pissarro-the-crystal-palace.fact: Pissarro learned from Courbet and Corot, and shaped both Impressionism and Post-Impressionism.

renoir-chrysanthemums.fact: Renoir has been called “the final representative of a tradition which runs directly from Rubens to Watteau.”

cezanne-the-basket-of-apples.fact: Cézanne bent the objects to show several viewpoints at once, an idea that fed Fauvism and Cubism.

sargent-thistles.fact: Sargent made roughly 900 oil paintings and more than 2,000 watercolors.

cezanne-the-bay-of-marseille-seen-from-l.fact: Cézanne’s work is the bridge between 19th-century Impressionism and early 20th-century Cubism.

cezanne-auvers-panoramic-view.fact: Cézanne’s new ways of representing the world shaped the avant-garde of the early 20th century.

sisley-the-seine-at-port-marly-piles-of-.fact: In 1907 the dealer Durand-Ruel tried to auction this painting, and failed.

sisley-watering-place-at-marly.fact: Among Sisley’s most important works is his series on the floods at Marly-le-Roi in 1875.

van-gogh-fishing-in-spring-the-pont-de-c.fact: Van Gogh’s 1887 paintings of Asnières mark a breakthrough in his development as an artist.

hokusai-shower-below-the-summit.fact: The Thirty-six Views were such a success that ten more prints were added to the series.

homer-breaking-storm-coast-of-maine.fact: Homer is considered one of the foremost painters of 19th-century America.

hiroshige-evening-snow-at-kanbara.fact: Hiroshige made this series after his first journey along the Tōkaidō road, in 1832.

van-gogh-grapes-lemons-pears-and-apples.fact: In Paris, Van Gogh transformed the subjects, colors and techniques of his still lifes.

courbet-the-brook-of-les-puits-noir.fact: Courbet led the Realist movement, committed to painting only what he could see.

sisley-the-loire.fact: Born in Paris to British parents, Sisley painted almost nothing but landscapes.

sisley-a-turn-in-the-road.fact: Sisley is considered the most consistent of the Impressionists in painting outdoors, en plein air.

courbet-an-alpine-scene.fact: Courbet rejected academic convention, setting an example for the Impressionists and the Cubists.

sargent-olive-trees-corfu.fact: Sargent’s travels took him from Venice to the Tyrol, Corfu, Capri, Spain, the Middle East, Montana, Maine and Florida.
